metadata.schema_version: v4 (v3 8D + degree-2 geodesy: C20/C22 observables + sampled non-hydrostaticity dC20_nh/dC22_nh) — clipper_v4_geodesy_11D
metadata.description: Europa Clipper v4 geodesy campaign: v3 8D (rheology + Tb_K + log10_wOcean_ppt salinity + sampled core, mass-conservation rho_sil) PLUS Mazarico-projected degree-2 gravity. Adds two sampled non-hydrostatic offsets dC20_nh, dC22_nh (uniform [-2e-5, 2e-5]) => 10 sampled parameters. k2 conditioning tightened to the Mazarico et al. (2023) projected precision (Re_k2 0.23+/-0.015, Im_k2 0.0040+/-0.015) replacing v1-v3's requirement-level sigma 0.06. CMR2 is RETAINED but RELABELED as a Galileo-derived MoI PRIOR (GC21 Table 3), not a Clipper observable. C20/C22 modeled directly via a hydrostatic Clairaut forward map (gravity_forward_model='clairaut_hydrostatic') + sampled non-hydrostatic offsets; the posterior of (dC20_nh, dC22_nh) IS the inferred degree of non-hydrostaticity. Same 2D (Tb x w) v3.0 structure cache (NO PP runs). Plan: plans/europa-clipper-v4-geodesy-plan.md.
metadata.gravity_forward_model_2026_07_19: gravity_forward_model='clairaut_hydrostatic' (InferenceConfig top-level flag). The C20/C22 observables are COMPUTED per sample by MCMCRunner._derive_gravity_pair: fluid Love number k_f by direct Clairaut integration (gravity_obs.clairaut_kf) over the SAME per-sample composite density profile the CMR2 mass-conservation derivation assembles (sampled core + derived silicate + cached hydrosphere; side-channel _last_composite_layers so they cannot diverge), then C22_h = k_f q_r / 4 rescaled to the GC21 1565 km reference radius, C20_h = -3.324 C22_h (Tricarico 2014 rapid-rotation ratio; classical 10/3 in docstrings only), plus the sampled offsets: C20_model = C20_h + dC20_nh, C22_model = C22_h + dC22_nh. Clairaut (not Radau-Darwin) is used because the ~1% RD systematic (~1e-6 in C22 = 5x sigma(C22)) would alias into the non-hydrostaticity deliverable (scientific review R2, 2026-07-19). RD retained only as a unit-test cross-check and the GUI inverse readout.
metadata.gravity_convention_2026_07_19: UNNORMALIZED Stokes coefficients (Anderson et al. 1998 / Gomez Casajus et al. 2021 convention), quoted at the GC21 reference radius R_ref = 1565 km (NOT the physical R_body = 1560.8 km; Clm scale as (R/R_ref)^2, a ~0.5% effect on C22 = 3x sigma(C22), applied in gravity_obs.hydrostatic_c20_c22). Fully-normalized conversions: C20_unnorm = sqrt(5) C_bar20; C22_unnorm = sqrt(10/24) C_bar22 ~ 0.6455 C_bar22. Hydrostatic ratio J2_h/C22_h = 3.324 (Tricarico 2014, as applied by GC21), NOT the classical synchronous 10/3.
metadata.gravity_fiducial_2026_07_19: C20 = -4.579201e-4, C22 = 1.377618e-4 (unnormalized, 1565 km). COMPUTED (not Anderson's numbers) at the v3 fiducial node via MCMCRunner._derive_gravity_pair with dC20_nh = dC22_nh = 0 and the v3 reference-MCMC posterior-median interior (alpha 0.3127, log10_zeta -0.197, log10_eta_Ih 12.938, log10_eta_sil 20.096, Tb 264.5 K, log10_wOcean 1.5460 = 35.165 ppt, R_core 534.67 km, rho_core 6254 kg/m^3). Self-consistent hydrostatic fiducial with zero-centered nuisances => the null test is clean (recovered non-hydrostaticity should be consistent with 0). Verified: -C20/C22 = 3.32400 exactly; q_r = 4.978e-4; implied k_f = 1.113 => RD C/MR2 = 0.35496 ~ GC21 MoI 0.3547. Evidence: plans/scripts/v4_fiducial_gravity.py, plans/scripts/v4_fiducial_gravity.json.
metadata.gravity_sigma_convention_risk_2026_07_19: sigma(C22) = 2.0e-7, sigma(C20) = 8.5e-7 (top of the Mazarico projected (3.5-8.5)e-7 range). Convention risk (USER ANSWER (a), 2026-07-19): if Table 5's sigma is 4-pi-normalized, unnorm sigma(C22) = 1.29e-7 (so 2.0e-7 is CONSERVATIVE) and unnorm sigma(C20) = 13.4e-7 (so 8.5e-7 carries a residual ~1.6x too-tight risk, documented). Non-hydrostaticity is an upper-limit deliverable whose floor is set by the MoI prior (moi_prior below, ~5-9e-6 in C22-equivalent), NOT by sigma(C22)=2e-7, so this residual sigma ambiguity does not drive the science claim.

moi_prior.note: The CMR2 observable [0.3547, 0.0024] IS this Galileo-era MoI, derived from GC21's C22 via Radau + hydrostatic assumption. RELABELED as a PRIOR (user 2026-07-19 (e)), independent of the future Clipper C20/C22 measurement the new observables represent => no double-counting. Restores the interior MoI constraint the review flagged as lost when gravity goes non-hydrostatic (R3). Swap Anderson (0.3475 +/- 0.0026) or Jacobson (0.3405 +/- 0.0022) here for sensitivity.

metadata.k2_provenance_2026_07_19: Re_k2 = 0.23 +/- 0.015, Im_k2 = 0.0040 +/- 0.015 (USER 2026-07-19, Mazarico et al. 2023 SSRv 219:30 sec 3.1.1). Central Re_k2 = 0.23 is the ocean-consistent value (Moore & Schubert 2000: 'around 0.23 with an ocean and <0.015 without'); sigma = 0.015 is the mid of the projected (1.4-1.8)e-2 49-flyby precision, REPLACING v1-v3's requirement-level sigma 0.06. Im_k2 central = 0.23 x sin(1 deg) = 0.0040 (1-degree phase-lag equivalent for a non-dissipative mantle; partial melt raises it, 1 deg is the adopted conditioning value); sigma = 0.015 (same as amplitude; the paper projects no separate phase uncertainty). h2 unchanged from v1-v3 (Re_h2 1.2+/-0.1, Im_h2 0+/-0.1).
metadata.primary_constraint: k2 (Mazarico-projected, 4x tighter than v3) + induction; CMR2 as Galileo MoI prior. Degree-2 gravity WITHOUT the hydrostatic assumption carries essentially zero interior information after marginalizing the two free nuisances (review R3); the interior comes from k2/h2/induction + the MoI prior.
metadata.non_hydrostaticity_deliverable_2026_07_1: The posterior of (dC20_nh, dC22_nh) is 'the degree of non-hydrostaticity implied' (user ask). Only the RATIO-BREAKING combination dC22_nh + (1/3.324) dC20_nh is identifiable; the ratio-preserving combination dC20_nh = -3.324 dC22_nh (hydrostatic-manifold tangent) is exactly degenerate with a C_bar shift. (Uses the Tricarico R=3.324 consistently, NOT the classical 10/3: the forward map is C20 = -3.324 C22_h + dC20_nh, so the identifiable/degenerate directions are set by 3.324; scientific-reviewer binding fix 2026-07-19.) Report: (dC20_nh, dC22_nh) posteriors in absolute units and in units of the Clipper sigmas, the implied -C20/C22 ratio vs 3.324, and the dC22_nh-C_bar posterior correlation. Pre-registered as an upper-limit measurement (GC21 C22=139e-6+/-25e-6 without hydrostatic assumption vs Anderson 131.5e-6 hydrostatic: a 0.36-sigma offset, CONSISTENT with hydrostatic). Prior sensitivity on the [-2e-5, 2e-5] nuisance box pre-registered (as for salinity).
metadata.salinity_prior_2026_07_18: log10_wOcean_ppt ~ Uniform[-1, 2] (0.1-100 ppt), log-uniform (Jeffreys). Report dual-space posteriors + prior-sensitivity; expect weak w identification and a Tb<->w degeneracy (synodic Ae saturated; w carried by orbital channels). The tighter v4 k2 sigma sharpens rheology/Tb marginals; the Tb-w ridge is induction-driven and should persist.
metadata.salinity_eos_caveat_2026_07_18: GSW/PSS-78 seawater EOS calibrated to SP<=42; 42-100 ppt extrapolation. Phase-1 gate (Pan et al. 2021 NaCl): max |dSigma| = 18.5% over a Europa column at w in {35,50,70,100} ppt, composition-dominated, all < the 25% caveat gate => 100 ppt bound KEPT. See plans/europa-clipper-v3-phase1-validation.md.
metadata.salinity_w_interp_caveat_2026_07_18: 16-node log-w grid introduces a 0.285 K support-edge w-interpolation bias at seawater (0.099 K worst-case over supported w); present IDENTICALLY in the reference MCMC and the SBI training set (both route through grid_interp_2d), so it does NOT break the degeneracy gate. Do not over-interpret the w support boundary to better than ~0.3 K / ~0.05 dex. See v3 config + plans/europa-clipper-v3-phase1-validation.md.
metadata.valid_region_2026_07_18: Valid (Tb, w) region is a TILTED BAND (None in both opposite corners of the 2D cache); bilinear lookup drops None corners and renormalizes, rejecting only when all 4 corners are None. CMR2 is flat (~0.346) across the valid region at all w => CMR2 does NOT constrain salinity; w rests on induction (orbital Ae).
metadata.bind_channels_provenance_2026_07_14: Induction observables unchanged from v3 (see europa_seawater_andrade_clipper_v3_8D.json). Bind = Ae*Be (UNCONJUGATED Ae, complex Be, FT surface-field path), sigma = 1.5 nT/channel; synodic |Ae|>0.7 support cut is the Galileo prior support, the Bind_synodic Gaussians are the Clipper likelihood.
metadata.core_bounds_rationale: R_core in [0, 0.5 R_body]; rho_core in [5000, 8000] kg/m^3 (metallic Fe / Fe-S); rho_sil derived from M_total mass conservation, samples outside [2200, 3500] kg/m^3 rejected.

metadata.zeta_split_2026_07_19: log10_zeta split into log10_zeta_Ih (ice Ih) and log10_zeta_sil (silicate), both U[-3, 2] (user 2026-07-19): a SINGLE sampled zeta couples the Andrade transient-creep amplification of ice and rock, so any zeta raised to fit ice dissipation (Im k2) simultaneously amplifies silicate dissipation - systematically preferencing silicate heating in the posterior heating budget. Independent zetas let the data set each. No HP-ice zeta: the Europa Tb box has no III/V/VI layers. Forward-model hook apply_andrade_params already supports per-phase zeta (log10_zeta_Ih/log10_zeta_sil override precedence).
